purpose: Freeze the fail-closed Rust behavior for current candidates, independent verification, exact evidence, computed verdicts, and bounded precise rework before implementation starts.

rustTarget.note: The rule and old-behavior audit always run. Named Rust modules and tests become mandatory once the phase 2.4 candidate module exists.

evidence.sourcePolicy: EvidenceRef stores a bounded source reference. Resolution must find one unique earlier source fact whose type, role, session identities, stage, and candidate all match; it never copies complete logs or command output.

verification.sessionPolicy: Reviewer and Verifier each use their own role-scoped StageRun and SessionBinding, distinct from the candidate writer and from one another.

verdict.computedBy: Rust Control Plane from current canonical Delivery state and exact Worker/Codex source facts; callers and Workers do not submit EvidenceRef, CriterionResult, or DeliveryVerdict objects.

rework.afterWriterStarts: The previous candidate immediately stops being current. Historical evidence may remain append-only, but it cannot authorize a new pass, review, or publication.

rules.statement: A frozen candidate is a deterministic derived value bound to the current DeliverySpec, repository baseline, one succeeded executor or remediator StageRun, its exact SessionBinding, and exact Git commit, tree, diff, and changed-path facts.

tests.name: freezes exact producer Git facts without creating another persisted domain object

rules.statement: A frozen candidate is stale after its spec identity or facts change, or as soon as a later executing or reworking writer StageRun starts, whether that writer is running or finished.

tests.name: invalidates prior acceptance and candidate identities after definition or writer changes

rules.statement: Reviewer and Verifier are both mandatory verification roles; a caller cannot remove either role, while an adversarial verifier remains an optional additional role.

tests.name: rejects malformed finding payloads and caller attempts to omit required roles

rules.statement: Reviewer and Verifier each bind one role-scoped verification StageRun to a complete SessionBinding; both are distinct from the candidate writer and from one another.

tests.name: binds exact approved inputs to separate existing reviewer and verifier sessions

typescript.gap: The old implementation rejects reuse of the producer SessionBinding and its DSH/Codex identities, but does not contain one direct negative test that reuses the same DSH/Codex identities across Reviewer and Verifier bindings. Rust must reject that cross-role reuse.

rules.statement: Every Reviewer, Verifier, and required adversarial verifier uses the canonical candidate-read-only workspace policy and a restricted runtime permission profile.

tests.name: requires a read-only verification role and rejects any successful verifier write

rules.statement: Any successful file or patch write observed in a verification Session invalidates that verification result; the candidate identity can only come from the original executor or remediator freeze.

tests.name: rejects foreign result identities, role drift, and verifier writes
requires a read-only verification role and rejects any successful verifier write

rules.statement: Every persisted EvidenceRef identifies the current Delivery and exact current DeliverySpec identity and revision.

tests.name: resolves runtime and Git facts to exact spec, candidate, stage, and session identities
invalidates prior acceptance and candidate identities after definition or writer changes

rules.statement: Every persisted EvidenceRef and every CriterionResult that cites it identify the exact current candidate; evidence for a prior or foreign candidate stays historical and cannot enter the current verdict.

tests.name: rejects missing, foreign, type-mismatched, and candidate-mismatched source facts
rejects stale acceptance, stale candidate, and foreign result identities

rules.statement: Every EvidenceRef identifies one existing Codex StageRun in the same Delivery, and a verification source must consume the producer candidate for the same DeliveryTask scope.

tests.name: resolves runtime and Git facts to exact spec, candidate, stage, and session identities

rules.statement: Every EvidenceRef identifies one SessionBinding for its StageRun, with complete session identities and a binding time that does not follow the evidence or predate the run.

tests.name: resolves runtime and Git facts to exact spec, candidate, stage, and session identities
rejects missing, foreign, type-mismatched, and candidate-mismatched source facts

rules.statement: A runtime EvidenceRef resolves to exactly one earlier source fact whose source type, ProductSession, WorkerSession, CodexThread, StageRun, role, sequence, and candidate identity all agree with the canonical SessionBinding.

tests.name: rejects missing, foreign, type-mismatched, and candidate-mismatched source facts
rejects foreign result identities, role drift, and verifier writes

typescript.gap: The old TypeScript source checks DSH Session and Codex Session identities. The Rust target replaces that backend pair with the canonical ProductSession, WorkerSession, CodexThread, StageRun, role, and source-sequence identity set from the phase-one contract.

rules.statement: A pass or fail CriterionResult cites at least one current EvidenceRef; inconclusive and infra_error may be evidence-free when the missing or failed verification state itself is the reason.

tests.name: fails closed for each non-passing verification condition

typescript.gap: The old higher-level computation test covers missing direct evidence, but there is no direct parser test for an evidence-free caller-created pass or fail result. Rust must test the invariant at its public domain constructor.

rules.statement: The current DeliveryVerdict evaluates every current acceptance criterion exactly once and includes no duplicate or foreign criterion.

tests.name: computes one deterministic passing verdict from current direct evidence

typescript.gap: The old computation produces one result per criterion, but its public tests do not directly submit a verdict with one missing, duplicate, or foreign criterion. Rust must test all three cases.

rules.statement: A missing, waiting, running, or incomplete required Reviewer or Verifier Session produces an inconclusive CriterionResult and cannot open the pass path.

tests.name: keeps missing, running, and optional adversarial settlements visible
fails closed for each non-passing verification condition

rules.statement: A settled finding without enough current direct evidence is inconclusive, records an evidence-mismatch finding, and cannot be changed into pass by the role message.

tests.name: fails closed for each non-passing verification condition

rules.statement: Different current Reviewer and Verifier conclusions for the same criterion preserve both findings, create a deterministic conflict record, and produce inconclusive for that criterion.

tests.name: projects independent settlements and preserves contradictory findings
fails closed for each non-passing verification condition

rules.statement: A failed or cancelled required verification Session, or timed-out, policy-denied, infrastructure-failed, or cancelled supporting execution, produces infra_error rather than pass, fail, or generic inconclusive.

tests.name: keeps timeout, policy denial, task failure, and infrastructure failure distinct
fails closed for each non-passing verification condition

rules.statement: A finding that claims pass while its cited test or command failed is an evidence mismatch and becomes inconclusive; an observed failed check can never support pass.

tests.name: fails closed for each non-passing verification condition

rules.statement: Precise rework is accepted only for the current reviewed candidate, exact diff, original DeliveryTask scope, visible diagram node, changed file, exact hunk digest, and current candidate-bound evidence references.

tests.name: StrongFlowService can hand a failed verdict through rework into a new verification run

rules.statement: A rework writer is a Codex remediator, the Control Plane derives its next attempt, and the number of rework StageRuns never exceeds the approved DeliverySpec maximum.

tests.name: Delivery accepts Delivery- or task-scoped Codex remediators within the approved limit
exhausted and repeated failures stop automatic code rework

rules.statement: Starting a new remediator writer immediately makes the previous frozen candidate non-current; the replacement binds a new StageRun and SessionBinding and must repeat Reviewer, Verifier, evidence, and verdict computation.

tests.name: invalidates prior acceptance and candidate identities after definition or writer changes
one browser action per role drives approved spec through both human review gates

rules.statement: When the approved rework limit is exhausted or the same criterion fails again after rework, the next action is definition clarification instead of another automatic code rework.

tests.name: exhausted and repeated failures stop automatic code rework
